note: Machine keys and values are ASCII-folded Turkish. `label` gives display text per language (tr with diacritics, en, de); `def` is the definition agents follow. The validator, the renderer and the reader app read this file; SCHEMA.md explains the rules around it.

block.syntax: one physical line: {key:value, key:"quoted value", ...}; enum values unquoted, everything else double-quoted; multiple values in one field are pipe-separated inside quotes
block.id_pattern: S<surah, 3 digits>-<kod of tur>-<NNN>, e.g. S107-HDS-001
block.placement: every record carries `paragraf`, the number of a prose paragraph of its page's base (numbered from 1 as in v16's augment; headings and Kaynaklar lines unnumbered), and `capa`, at least three exact words of that paragraph confirming the number. The block is rendered right after that paragraph. There are no end-of-page blocks: a record whose number is out of range or whose capa is not in that paragraph is dropped. Both passes number the same frozen base, so their blocks merge by paragraph.

gelenek.def: which literature the block belongs to; one per block. The Islamic pass stamps islami (the script adds it); in the Bible pass each block is tevrat or incil

tur.def: what kind of information the block carries

ayet.def: the ayah or range of this page the block is about: "107:3", "107:1-3"; several with |. Other passages the block cites go in metin and kaynak, not here

islev.def: why the block stands at this point of the page

iliski.def: how the cited source relates to this ayah

durum.def: epistemic status of the block's claim relative to its source

metin.def: the block's prose, in the page language, within the word limit of its layer

kaynak.def: source locators, pipe-separated: <ID>:<locator> exactly as in the corpus (TAB:107:3, MUSLIM:2985, ELMALILI:107:2, LISAN:دعع), or "hafiza" for model memory; Bible locators use OSIS book abbreviations (WLC:Gen.22.2, SBLGNT:Matt.6.5)

guc.def: strength of a connection to the project's reading

klasik_tanik.def: how far a project finding is attested in the checked sources; on a yenilik block, or on the oncul block of an attested finding

tarama.def: whether the check ran over the per-ayah slice only or over whole-book texts

derece.def: hadith/report grade; hadis blocks accept only sahih

derece_veren.def: who grades it: Buhârî | Müslim for the Sahihayn, named graders for other books (as the corpus records them); empty only with derece:degerlendirilmedi

tarihsellik.def: historical standing of an event or chronology claim

sozluk.def: which lexicon(s) the observation comes from, pipe-separated corpus IDs; PROJE = the project dictionary (../dictionary via quran-data); modern Arabic dictionaries only inside anlam_tarihi

mutercim.def: meal source ID (MEAL-OKUYAN), several with |, or "ortak" for a loss shared across the panel

terim.def: the Arabic word or expression in question

yon.def: loss or gain; a relay step can be both against different poles

kiyas.def: the pole a meal is judged against: the Arabic, or the intermediate text it was translated from

taban.def: exact short quote of the base text being corrected; must occur verbatim in the base

hata.def: kind of error in the base

koken.def: earliest traceable source of a report

tekrar.def: later works repeating the same report unchanged, pipe-separated IDs

gerekce.def: reason for a rejection or a grade

bag.def: what the block claims about the link between the Qur'an and the other text; a parallel is not a dependence, so the weakest fitting value is used

tarihleme.def: date of the cited text relative to the Qur'an (as the scholarship dates it)

nusha.def: the witness or text family quoted; readings differ, and the Qur'an's closest match may be the Syriac or Greek, not the Hebrew. Pipe-separated when several are compared

islami.def: the Islamic-literature pass: tafsir, hadith, lexica, meals and the rest of the main corpus

tevrat.def: the Hebrew Bible in any witness (Masoretic, Septuagint, Peshitta, Targum), the Psalms (Zebur) included; Jewish pseudepigrapha; Mishnah, Talmud, midrash

incil.def: the New Testament in any witness (Greek, Peshitta, Diatessaron); Christian apocrypha (Protevangelium of James, Infancy Gospels); Church Fathers; Syriac homilies. A Hebrew Bible text read through Christian exegesis is two blocks: the text (tevrat), its Christian reading (incil)

tefsir_rivayet.def: explanations of Companions/Successors as transmitted (Mujāhid, Muqātil, Ṭabarī's aqwāl, al-Durr al-manthūr)

tefsir_dirayet.def: an exegete's own analysis: language, reasoning, theology (Zamakhsharī, Rāzī, Ibn ʿĀshūr, Elmalılı, Kur'an Yolu)

isari.def: ishārī readings (Qushayrī, Sulamī, Tustarī, Bursevî); labelled as such, never as dirayet

nazm.def: sequence, adjacency, surah unity, surah-to-surah relation; structural form (ring, symmetry, rhyme groups) with islev:yapi

nuzul.def: Makkī/Madanī, revelation order and chronology lists (Itqān, Ibn ʿĀshūr; Nöldeke, Neuwirth reported beside them)

esbab.def: isnād-bearing occasion reports of any grade, each with derece and tarihsellik shown

hadis.def: Prophetic hadith; sahih only (Bukhārī, Muslim, or sunan reports every named grader calls sahih)

kiraat.def: canonical and non-canonical readings and their linguistic justification (ḥujja)

lugat.def: synchronic lexical evidence: senses, branches, the lexica's own wording and shawāhid

vucuh.def: the senses a word takes across the Qur'an, from the wujūh wa-naẓāʾir books (Muqātil, Dāmghānī, Ibn al-Jawzī) and the usage table

nahiv.def: syntax, iʿrāb, morphology that bears on meaning

belagat.def: rhetoric, majāz, imagery, iʿjāz theory (Zamakhsharī, Jurjānī, Asās)

ayet_ayet.def: a Qur'anic passage that explains, extends or contrasts this one

anlam_tarihi.def: diachronic change only: pre-Qur'anic → Qur'anic → later Arabic → Turkish loanword drift

tarihi_baglam.def: sourced setting: sīra, Mecca, material culture, institutions

meal.def: how Turkish (and relay) translations render a term: what they keep, lose or add

modern.def: modern Islamic and Western scholarship, kept apart from classical attestation

yenilik.def: how far a finding of the base is attested, written only when no antecedent was found (klasik_tanik bulunamadi or yapitaslari); an attested finding carries klasik_tanik on its oncul block. At most one per paragraph; always kat:arastirma

paralel.def: the same figure, scene or story told in the other scripture (Abraham's sacrifice, Joseph, the sleepers)

motif.def: a shared image, formula or ethical motif without a shared story (praying to be seen: Mt 6:5 and 107:6)

karsi_anlati.def: the Qur'an tells it differently, corrects or answers it (Mary, the crucifixion, the calf); the difference is the point

soydas.def: a Hebrew, Aramaic or Syriac cognate of the Qur'anic word and how the other scripture uses it; loan claims only with named scholarship

yorum_gelenegi.def: Jewish or Christian interpretation of the parallel text (Targum, midrash, Talmud; Church Fathers, Syriac homilies such as Ephrem and Jacob of Serugh)

elenen.def: a connection considered and rejected, kept for audit

kaynak_notu.def: source criticism: provenance, attribution, edition, isnād caveats

yontem.def: a methodological limit or distinction the reader needs here

duzeltme.def: an error in the frozen base: wrong label, quotation, ayah number, fact or rendering; also logged to errata.jsonl

erken_tanik.def: an early attestation of an interpretation or sense

aciklama.def: clarifies wording, grammar, referent or a distinction

destek.def: independently supports a reading already on the page

oncul.def: a source that already states (part of) a finding of the base

itiraz.def: an argument that a reading of the base cannot hold here (grammar, near-synonymy, root identity, reading); not a mere preference

tercih.def: a source's stated preference among readings ("the correct view is X"); reported, not adjudicated

tasnif.def: a source lists several senses without choosing (Māwardī, Ibn al-Jawzī)

anlam_alani.def: several live senses of a word or expression

gelisim.def: how an interpretation or sense changed over time

sinir.def: what the ayah or a reading does not say; prevents an overreading

karsit.def: an opposite or counter-scene that sharpens the reading

sonuc.def: why a distinction matters for understanding

fazilet.def: reports on the merit of a surah or ayah

yapi.def: formal structure: ring, symmetry, rhyme groups, parallelism

dogrudan.def: the source explicitly treats this ayah or phrase (Bible pass: a text the scholarship reads as directly addressed by this ayah)

tematik.def: same theme, not an explanation of this ayah

lafzi.def: linked through the same word, root or expression

yapisal.def: linked through position, sequence or form

karsilastirmali.def: a comparison across sources, readings or translations

aktarilan.def: the source transmits it; its truth is not established

yorum.def: an interpretive synthesis (the base's or the block's)

degerlendirilmedi.def: not checked against a source; required for model memory

temel.def: shown by default: what an advanced reader should see first at that point

arastirma.def: hidden by default (the reader opens it): audit trail, novelty detail, rejected candidates, technical source criticism

dogrudan.def: direct support for the reading in context

guclu.def: a strongly illuminating link that is not the primary meaning

ikincil.def: a legitimate secondary resonance that keeps the primary meaning intact

acik.def: the same connection is stated in a checked source

kismi.def: an important part is stated; the base adds the rest

yapitaslari.def: the ingredients are attested separately; the combination is not

bulunamadi.def: no parallel in the listed sources; never an absolute claim

dilim.def: only the per-ayah texts of this surah were searched; a negative result is weak

tam.def: whole-book texts were searched across the Qur'an

sahabe.def: a reading reported from a Companion's codex, often explanatory

kelime.def: a different concept (ṣudūr rendered as kalp)

eleman.def: a preposition, pronoun, number, emphasis, conjunction or voice the Turkish could have kept

aralik.def: several live senses narrowed to one

ekleme.def: the translator's own words presented as the text

kayma.def: a loanword whose Turkish sense has shifted (namaz, din, ibadet)

isaretleme.def: brackets, italics or notes changed so an addition no longer looks like one

aktarma.def: a difference that comes from translating an intermediate text (Asad's English, Mawdudi's Urdu), not the Arabic

kayip.def: the translation loses against the pole

kazanc.def: the translation recovers something against the pole

ara_metin.def: judged against the text it was translated from

kaynak_etiketi.def: a wrong source or lexicon label

ceviri.def: a wrong rendering of the Arabic

benzerlik.def: the texts resemble each other; nothing is claimed about a relation (the default)

ortak_havza.def: both draw on a tradition current in Late Antiquity; no direction claimed

muhatap.def: named scholarship argues the Qur'an addresses, answers or corrects this tradition; requires alim

etki_iddiasi.def: named scholarship argues dependence; reported as that scholar's claim, never as fact; requires alim; impossible for a text dated after the Qur'an

kuran_oncesi.def: written down before the early 7th century

kuran_sonrasi.def: redacted after the Qur'an (e.g. Pirqe de-Rabbi Eliezer); may preserve older material, which the block must argue

pesitta.def: the Syriac Bible, Old and New Testament

targum.def: Aramaic renderings of the Hebrew Bible

diatessaron.def: Tatian's gospel harmony, through its witnesses

suryani.def: Syriac homilies and hymns (Ephrem, Jacob of Serugh, Narsai)

rules.def: tur:hadis requires derece:sahih and derece_veren naming Buhârî, Müslim or the graders recorded in the corpus; merit (fazilet) reports are hadith and follow the same rule; a weak Prophetic attribution of a sound Companion statement is reported as the Companion's (tefsir_rivayet)
kaynak:hafiza (or a corpus source with access hafiza) requires durum:degerlendirilmedi; forbidden for tur hadis and nuzul, for derece, and for Turkish loanword history in anlam_tarihi
a source preferring another reading is islev:tercih; islev:itiraz needs an argument that the base's reading cannot hold here
klasik_tanik:bulunamadi with tarama:dilim must say in metin that only the per-ayah slice was searched
modern Arabic dictionaries (VASIT, MUHIT, HANSWEHR) may be cited only in anlam_tarihi, as evidence of later drift
every block names its prose paragraph (paragraf) and quotes at least three words of it (capa); it is rendered right after that paragraph; a block whose number and words do not match is dropped

each block belongs to one gelenek and its tur must allow it. islami blocks cite no Bible, Jewish or Christian source (kind intertext); tevrat and incil blocks cite only sources of their own gelenek, plus the Qur'an text and modern scholarship. The passes run separately and never read each other's records
a parallel is not a dependence: bag defaults to benzerlik; muhatap and etki_iddiasi require alim and a source that argues it; etki_iddiasi is impossible with tarihleme:kuran_sonrasi
a separate yenilik block only when no antecedent was found, kat:arastirma, at most one per paragraph; an attested finding carries klasik_tanik/taranan/tarama on its oncul block
blocks are read right after their paragraph: no 'taban' in metin (say şerh or state the point), no closing disclaimers, each point once on the page, at most five blocks after one paragraph
